title: I Watched Birds Grow Up in My Backyard—You Can Too!
summary:
Have you ever wondered what goes on inside a birdhouse? Well, one reviewer found out—and now you can too! The Birdfy Nest Duo is a smart nest box with two cameras: one inside and one outside. It lets you watch birds build their nest, lay eggs, and raise their babies, all from your phone!

The reviewer set up the box in her backyard in March. Soon, a black-capped chickadee moved in. She watched the bird dig out the nest, gather moss, and add a layer of fur. Then the mom laid seven eggs! The dad brought her moths and green inchworms to eat.

All seven eggs hatched, but only four babies survived. One night, the reviewer saw the mom carry a baby out of the nest and not come back with it. It was sad, but that's nature.

The box also measures temperature and humidity. During a heat wave, the temperature inside got up to 96 degrees Fahrenheit—that's dangerous for baby birds. The reviewer had to put ice packs on top to cool it down.

She learned lots of cool stuff: chickadees feed their babies spiders because they have taurine, which helps brains grow. And baby birds poop in little 'packets' that the mom removes to keep the nest clean.

The Birdfy Nest Duo isn't cheap, but it's like having your own nature documentary. If you love birds, this could be the coolest thing ever!
why_it_matters: Seeing a bird family this close can make kids more curious about nature and remind us that animals face dangers like heat and predators.

background_read: Black-capped chickadees (tiny birds with black heads and white cheeks) normally nest in holes in trees.
People can put up nest boxes to give them a safe place, and a camera inside lets you watch the whole family.
Watching birds this closely helps us understand things like what baby birds eat and how parents keep the nest clean.
Article_Structure: WHO: A reviewer and a black-capped chickadee family.
WHAT: The reviewer used a smart nest box with two cameras to watch the birds build a nest, lay eggs, and raise babies.
WHY: To show people that they can watch nature up close and learn surprising things about birds.

perspectives.description: They get to see real bird life through the cameras, like the bird digging out the nest and feeding babies.
It can be sad—one baby didn't survive and heat can be dangerous—so nature isn't always easy to watch.
The Birdfy Nest Duo isn't cheap, and a camera can't replace helping wild birds have safe natural spaces.
